core_job: Safe Walk, for a woman walking somewhere alone, usually at night. She sets how long the walk should take and taps Start walk. Kinnav opens a pre-written SMS to her chosen safety contacts with her ETA and location, and starts a countdown that is persisted and backed by two local notifications, so it still reaches her when the phone is locked. She taps I'm safe when she arrives. If she doesn't, the deadline notification fires, and after a grace period a second one opens the alert text with a fresh location, ready to send. A confirmed emergency dial is on screen throughout. Every walk is saved to a history she can search, filter, annotate and export. The honest limit: iOS and Android do not let an app send a text by itself, so the user taps Send, and the app never claims anyone was alerted.
signature: Safe Havens: nearby places that are staffed and open now (police, emergency departments, pharmacies, late-opening shops), from the keyless OpenStreetMap Overpass API. Each row has a compass arrow and distance from the user's GPS position. Open-now status is parsed on-device from the opening_hours tag and is never guessed (it shows "unknown" when the tag can't be parsed). Walk there hands off to the phone's own maps app, so the app does no routing. Havens are pre-fetched and cached when a walk starts, so they still work offline or when the server is overloaded. Requests go one category at a time with a retry, and failures are shown per category, with a "Search Maps instead" fallback. Overpass check, 2026-10-12: 4 single-category queries returned 200 (NYC pharmacies: 12 results, 9 with opening_hours). All 3 union queries and 3 of 7 single queries returned 504. The fallback map URLs answered 301/200. Competitors were checked only by their store descriptions, via the keyless iTunes API (web search is disabled in this session): Noonlight, bSafe, Bond, Aster, Citizen. None of the descriptions offer a free list of open-now places to walk into; Bond's "safe place" is an agent arranging a car, listed under premium services. Apple's built-in Check In is marked "competitor not verified".
